_scene.caption: A career with two tiers it could commit to and one building already in the queue. The balance covers one of the two prices and not the other, and neither is refused: RP-1 bills a construction as it builds, so a short career gets a slower upgrade. That is carried by "over the build" beside each price and by "Commit" on the confirm rather than by a sentence about it. Each badge is the tier the building is AT, and it is the same number the grid above reads because it comes from the same place: on an RP-1 save this Uplink feeds the host's grid, so the two cannot be a second opinion. The step is the control's, and it says "Queue upgrade". The grid's own Upgrade controls read Blocked, because the tier they would buy is not for sale under RP-1 at all

emits.comment: RP-1's own answer to the tier question, which on an RP-1 save is the only right one: this Uplink contributes it into the host's grid ABOVE the host's own reading of career.facilities, so the grid draws these rows and not the stock ones. Without it the scene depicts a save where RP-1 is running and mute, the grid is empty because an empty contribution still holds the band, and no Upgrade control exists to carry the gate's refusal. MissionControl is here at upgradedByRp1 false on purpose: RP-1 prices it at a single fund under a cosmetic-only comment and drives its tier itself, so it gets a tier and never a price.

Rp1CareerProjectGate's standing verdict. Without it the picture shows a managed RP-1 career whose stock Upgrade buttons are live, which is a space centre RP-1 could never produce: the gate refuses career.facility.upgrade on every save RP-1 manages, and the section below is the act it names instead.

verdict.detail: RP-1 builds a facility upgrade as a construction project with its own cost and duration, so it has to be queued rather than bought outright. Use rp1.facility.upgrade
